newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens - no damage from Moody's downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Siemens - no damage from Moody's downgrade.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said on Friday it expected no worsening of its financial condition after Moody's downgraded the rating on its senior debt.
The company also said it expected productivity to improve nine to ten percent in the 1996/97 -- in response to Moody's saying productivity improvements so far have been insufficient.

"A worsening of the financial condition of Siemens is not to be expected" as a result of Moody's change, Siemens said in a statement. "We are disappointed in the basic opinion of the strategic steps by Siemens in the last few years."
Gains in productivity, which had been improving by three or four percent a few years ago, were accelerating and would lead to rising profits in the next few years, Siemens said.
The company went on to say its expansion into Asia has been very successful, tripling the region's revenues over the last several years to more than 15 billion marks ($8.6 billion).
